ai.title: CLI auth switches from WebSocket to HTTP endpoints
ai.summary: CLI authentication (login, status, logout) moves from WebSocket actions to HTTP REST endpoints at `/api/auth/cli/*`. This change improves reliability by decoupling auth flows from the persistent WebSocket connection. Updates span `npm-app/src/client.ts` (fetch calls), `web/src/app/api/auth/cli/*` (new routes), and `common/src/actions.ts` (removed WS schemas). CORS headers for `/api/auth/cli/:path*` are added in `web/next.config.mjs`.

eli5.text: When you log in, check your login status, or log out using the command-line tool, your computer now talks to the server using standard web requests instead of a constant live connection. This makes those actions more reliable, especially on unstable networks. If you looked at the tool, the login flow wouldn't appear to change, but the behind-the-scenes communication is more robust.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.164
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json bumped from 1.0.163 to 1.0.164. Internal release preparation for the codebuff package. No functional code changes in this commit.

eli5.text: Starting today, signing in to the assistant through a terminal command works over normal web traffic instead of a persistent real-time connection, making login, status checks, and logout more reliable. This change affects anyone who authenticates the assistant from the command line, and the new method began rolling out as part of this update. The package itself was also given a new internal version label so that installations pick up the latest files.

ai.title: Update Relace API endpoint to codebuff-instantapply
ai.summary: The Relace AI endpoint in `backend/src/relace-api.ts` changed from `instantapply.endpoint.relace.run` to `codebuff-instantapply.endpoint.relace.run`. This update reflects a shift in the upstream service routing for the code application feature. The change is isolated to the backend API client configuration.

eli5.text: When you trigger the code application feature, the system now sends your request to a different backend service address. If you looked at the network activity while using this feature, you would see the destination URL in the request changed from instantapply.endpoint.relace.run to codebuff-instantapply.endpoint.relace.run. This is a behind-the-scenes routing adjustment in how the service talks to its internal code application provider; you should not notice any difference in how the feature behaves. The change is live today.

ai.title: Upgrade coding agent
ai.summary: Updated hero section text in web/src/app/page.tsx to "Upgrade your coding agent" and added "Run in your terminal or IDE!" to the subtext. Replaced gradient text styling with solid blue. Added SWELancer-Benchmark submodule at commit af5d5dab1.

eli5.text: The main landing page of the app was updated with new headline text: 'Upgrade your coding agent' and a subtitle that says it can run in your terminal or IDE. The old gradient-colored title was replaced with a solid blue color. A new benchmark dataset was also added as a submodule to help evaluate AI coding performance. These changes affect anyone visiting the homepage or testing AI coding capabilities.

ai.title: Landing page CTA shows install command with copy button
ai.summary: web/src/app/page.tsx replaces generic Start Coding button with InstallCommand component showing `npm install -g codebuff` and clipboard copy via `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Copy state uses `useState` with 2s timeout, toggling `Check`/`Copy` icons from `lucide-react`. CTA section spacing tightened (`mb-32`→`mb-16`, `py-16`→`py-12`), subtitle text changed to "Start coding in less than a minute". PostHog event `home.cta_clicked` retained on step-by-step guide link with `location: 'cta_section'`.

eli5.text: If you visit the CodeBuff landing page today, the big call-to-action button at the bottom has been replaced with the actual command you need to run (`npm install -g codebuff`) inside a box that now has a copy icon beside it. When you click that icon, the command is copied to your clipboard and a green checkmark appears for two seconds to confirm it was copied, so you no longer have to manually select or type the install command yourself. The section is also visually tighter and its subtitle now reads 'Start coding in less than a minute', while the old 'Start Coding with AI' button still opens the install guide but no longer sits directly in this new install box.
